$comment: The shell's vocabulary check (mold_v0-045, scripts/check-vocabulary.ts, npm run check:vocabulary; the smoke test runs it too). `words`: the product words no file of the shell may carry, in any case, in its text or its path. Each `allow` entry lets one exact spelling stay, in the listed files only, and says what holds it: the old env prefix where the alias must name it, and names that outlive a release (a database's functions and roles, built images and boat templates, files on running orchestrator sandboxes), which only a migration of what holds them can rename. An entry that matches nothing fails the check too, so the list cannot outgrow what is there. `files`: whole files the check does not read, each with why. A pack's own files (packs/<id>/, web/src/packs/<id>/, orchestrator/packs/<id>/) and, in a build with packs, the generated files are the pack's and are not read.

files.sql/migrations/*.sql: applied migrations are checksummed (src/migrate.ts) and replayed on every new database: their text, comments included, stays as it was applied
files.scripts/fixtures/pre-049-migrations/*.sq: byte copies of the migrations as they were before mold_v0-049, the fixture test:migrations upgrades from
files.web/src/lib/octillion-format.ts: the module path host packs' console pages written before mold_v0-045 import; it only re-exports display-format.ts

allow.why: the env names' prefix before mold_v0-045, spelled once per place that reads the old names as a fallback (src/env-names.ts; the console's own copy; the console's build config; bootstrap.sh, which carries a .env's old names to the new ones)
a deploy script reading an env name, its old spelling as the fallback of the new one only

functions, the tenant role and its setting that sql/migrations created and that every row-level security policy on a live database names: renaming them is a migration of every policy (follow-up), not a rename
the tags of the coding agents' images and the sandbox image, already built on hosts and pinned in harnesses/registry.json (image.docker): a new tag needs every image rebuilt (follow-up)
the boat named snapshots (image.boat_snapshot) the harnesses' sandboxes start from, which exist under these names in the boat account

the orchestrator sandboxes' service unit, home and host marker, and the harness manifests in the boat templates: running sandboxes hold them, and the next release stops, restarts and checks those (boat-lib stopService, host-guard)
test data, never shipped: the first product's landing page written word for word as a landing block (mold_v0-122), so its own screenshots can check that the shell's section library reproduces it

names on the sandbox provider (boat) and its VMs that running fleets hold: the default namespace ("octi" on a server, "octv" on Vercel) every autoscaler reaps orphans by, the names of orchestrator, worker, pool and run sandboxes and snapshot images under it, and the unprivileged `octi` user baked into the snapshots. Renaming them is a rebuild of the snapshots and a namespace migration (mold_v0-097), not a rename

users, groups, paths and units on run sandboxes, orchestrator pods and runner hosts that a built image or a host already holds: the run users (octirun-*) and the egress proxy's user (octiproxy) the runner image creates, its tools directory, the uid leases and checkout cache that outlive a release on a runner's host, the proxy's logs and set-up paths, and the tests that check those exact names. Renamed with the image rebuild (mold_v0-097)

concepts.$comment: The concept-word ratchet (mold_v0-100, scripts/lib/concepts.ts; npm run check:vocabulary runs it). `words`: the first product's concepts, taken from its host pack (packs/octillion: pack.json description "Agentic Preference Optimization ... pick your developer tool", its host.schema tables products/scenarios/simulations/developer_profiles/developer_populations/product_personas/journey_templates/visibility_reports, its pick-rate and hit-rate reports and playbooks). None may stand as PROSE in base text (string literals, template text and JSX text of the shell's sources): base text writes a placeholder the build's words fill ({run}, {Runs}, {member}, {product}: src/words.ts), or leaves the concept to the host pack. Identifiers, SQL and stored values are contracts and are never counted. Each file that still carries one has a ceiling, the exact count today, in a group that says why it remains and how it goes; more fails, fewer fails with the number to lower it to.

skip.**/*.generated.*: generated from the packs and the profile (a host pack's own words land there in its build)
skip.src/words.ts: the words engine: its comments' examples name the words a pack may choose
skip.web/src/packs/**: a host pack's own console code (its files in a build), never the shell's

host_gated.why: Text shown only where the build's host pack has the feature or the tables (hostFeature('journeys'), hostFeature('research'), hostTable('products'), the session engine's tables): a declarative app never reaches it.
host_gated.migration: Moves into the host pack when the hook it sits behind gets a pack field (HostWeb/HostDefinition copy hooks; audit rows 7, 8 and 17).

host_tables.why: Labels and checks of the host pack's own tables (the storage page's table list, the row-level security probes), each guarded by hostTable(): stored names, read only in a build that has them.
host_tables.migration: Each table's label comes from the host pack's pack.json host.schema when it gets labels (follow-up of mold_v0-049).

account_funnel.why: The session engine's attention messages that no build word can say (its failed product research, its report), kept word for word in a build with that engine (audit row 7).
account_funnel.migration: Done for every other build (mold_v0-103): the shell's stages up to first_call, then the packs' onboarding[].done_when steps. These two go with a host pack hook for its own stages and messages.

admin_sections.why: Staff-only admin text that only the session engine's builds show and no build word can say: the attention message for its failed product research, its tip dialog, its plan template's example, its compute knobs and job kinds, its billing metric (audit row 8).
admin_sections.migration: Done on the console's pages (mold_v0-104): the engine's sections show only when sessionEngine() (web/src/features/admin/engine.ts), the packs' runs per job kind in their words otherwise. What is left goes with host pack hooks for its own texts.

usage_page.why: /app/usage is the first product's usage page (simulations run, hit rate), reachable by URL only in a declarative app, whose tabs send usage to /app/activity (audit row 14).
usage_page.migration: Redirect /app/usage to /app/activity when sessionEngine() is false, the page moving to the host pack (audit row 14 ticket).
